newsitem.title: USA: WISCONSIN ENERGY, NORTHERN STATES CALL OFF MERGER.
newsitem.headline: WISCONSIN ENERGY, NORTHERN STATES CALL OFF MERGER.

text.p: Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co announced late on Friday that they are calling off plans to merge.
The proposed $6 billion merger into a company called Primergy Corp would have formed the 10th largest investor-owned utility in the country.

But the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday said Wisconsin Energy and Northern States Power would have to sell some power plants and make major modifications before the deal could be approved.
The two companies announced on Friday they would pass on the merger rather than try to make it acceptable.
The merger also had been encountering difficulty with state regulators in Minnesota and Wisconsin.
Wisconsin Energy is based in Milwaukee. Northern States Power is based in Minneapolis. Primergy would have been based in Minneapolis.
When they announced the merger plans in May 1995, the companies said rates would be lower. But critics questioned that, given what would have been Primergy's dominance in the upper Midwest.
